finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice by ID with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken object-level authorization). The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> enforces inv['customer'] == g.user['id'], which shows the check is intended but missing here.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request path parameter inv_id (attacker-chosen or enumerated invoice ID)
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and any other invoice data, for any customer

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator or before_request hook
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the record by the attacker-supplied key; there is no comparison against the caller's identity
Full invoice is serialized and returned to the caller
For contrast, the /my/ route checks the owner here; the unscoped route does not

finding.guards_checked: Checked for a before_request/auth decorator, a g.user ownership comparison, and a role check on this route. None exist; the only file is invoices.py and it has no middleware. Routes are Flask defaults and publicly reachable. Not found: rate limiting or unguessable IDs (IDs are dict keys of unknown format).

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator, before_request hook or ownership check and returns jsonify(INVOICES.get(inv_id)), while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 compares inv["customer"] to g.user["id"]; no other files or middleware exist in the directory.
